html:
Kuwait became independent on 19 June 1961, when it ended the agreement of 1899 with Britain. Within days Iraq's leader Abd al-Karim Qasim claimed it as part of Iraq.

Britain answered with Operation Vantage, landing troops in July 1961 to deter an invasion. The Arab League then admitted Kuwait as a member and sent its own force, and the British left. Iraq recognised Kuwait in 1963 after Qasim fell.

Independence let the Al Sabah and the merchants build a state on their own terms, with a constitution and an elected assembly. Iraq's claim never quite died, and Saddam Hussein revived it in 1990 with the invasion.
sum: Kuwait became independent on 19 June 1961, when it ended the agreement of 1899 with Britain. Within days Iraq's leader Abd al-Karim Qasim claimed it as part of Iraq.
